content: Azelastine is an antihistamine medication prescribed to treat hay fever and allergy symptoms, such as a runny nose, sneezing, and an itchy nose. It may also be prescribed for other uses; consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Azelastine is available as a nasal spray. Typically, it is sprayed into each nostril twice daily. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Use azelastine exactly as directed. Do not use more or less of it or use it more frequently than prescribed by your doctor. Before using azelastine for the first time, remove the child-resistant screw cap and replace it with the pump unit. Prime the pump unit by spraying it four times or until a fine mist appears. If three or more days have passed since your last use, reprime the pump with two sprays or until a fine mist appears. Before using azelastine, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to azelastine or any other medications. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially other cold and allergy products, antihistamines, and vitamins. Notify your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while using azelastine, contact your doctor immediately. If you are undergoing surgery, including dental surgery, inform your doctor or dentist that you are using azelastine. Be aware that this medication may cause drowsiness. Avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how azelastine affects you. Alcohol can increase the drowsiness caused by this medication, so use caution. If you miss a dose, use it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not use a double dose to make up for a missed one. Azelastine may cause side effects. Notify your doctor if you experience any of the following symptoms, especially if they are severe or persistent: bitter taste, tiredness, weight gain, muscle pain, or nasal burning. Store this medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of any outdated or no longer needed medication properly. Consult your pharmacist for guidance on proper disposal. If a young child accidentally ingests azelastine, contact a doctor or poison control center immediately. Keep all appointments with your doctor. Do not share your medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, ask your pharmacist. It is important to maintain a written list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, including vitamins, minerals, and dietary supplements. Bring this list with you to every doctor’s visit or if you are admitted to a hospital. This information is also crucial in case of emergencies.
